https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: More Warhammer 40,000 detachments for Codex-compliant Chapters.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
Over the past few days we’ve been looking at updated rules for various Space Marine factions from the Blood Angels to the Black Templars that will be available once the upcoming Codex: Space Marines launches. Today, we’re finishing off with some of the more Codex-compliant Chapters who also get their own detachments.

Salamanders

The Salamanders have a very particular love of close-range firepower, and that returns in the renovated Forgefather’s Seekers detachment. Now that the Devastator doctrine from the new Combat Doctrines army rule lets you give your guns Assault anyway, this detachment lets you use that doctrine an additional time per game, while improving Vulkan He’stan’s effect on Infernus Squads by letting them perform actions after advancing or falling back. 

DETACHMENT RULES

VULKAN’S QUEST

Tireless in his pursuit of the Primarch’s legacy, Forgefather Vulkan He’stan annihilates any who impede his quest. Favouring swift, aggressive assaults, he and his warriors close rapidly with the enemy, destroying them at close range with ruthless efficiency.

  • You can select the devastator doctrine one additional time per battle.

  • Friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES units’ ranged attacks that target a unit within 12”, have +1 S.

If your army includes a VULKAN HE’STAN unit, friendly INFERNUS SQUAD units have the following:

  • When this unit is selected to make an advance/fall-back move, that advance/fall-back move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to start an action.

  • When this unit starts an action, that action does not prevent this unit from being eligible to shoot.

Restrictions: Your army can include SALAMANDERS units, but it cannot include any ADEPTUS ASTARTES units drawn from any other Chapter.

Changes to the way that common Torrent weapons like flamers work – now having a fixed number of shots with the Blast ability – means they can’t be fired while engaged even when fighting Vehicles and Monsters… unless you’re the Salamanders, who have spent the last 10,000 years shooting flamers at things and have gotten rather good at it. 

The Forged in Fire stratagem strips away all the downsides so you can cook your foes at point-blank range, and if you’d rather fall back before shooting instead, Wrath and Ruin activates an alternative doctrine for extra flexibility.

FORGED IN FIRE (1CP)

FORGEFATHER’S SEEKERS STRATAGEM

The Salamanders are masters of the flamer, wielding such weapons with supreme precision and utilising them even in the press of melee combat.

WHEN: Your Shooting phase, when a friendly engaged ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit is selected to shoot.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit. 

EFFECT: Your unit’s [TORRENT] weapons:

  • Do not have [BLAST].

  • Have [CLOSE-QUARTERS].

  • Have +1 A.

WRATH AND RUIN (1CP)

FORGEFATHER’S SEEKERS STRATAGEM

Having drawn their enemies in, Space Marine battle-brothers fall back and open fire at point-blank range before thundering forward to put any survivors to death.

WHEN: Your Command phase.

TARGET: One ADEPTUS ASTARTES infantry unit. 

EFFECT: The assault doctrine or tactical doctrine is active for your unit, until the start of your next Command phase.

Raven Guard

Now that Phobos-armoured units get a speed boost in return for lighter armour, the Raven Guard are masters of the movement game – and the Shadowmark Talon enhances their stealth so they can rush towards objectives with impunity. Where before they only got the Benefit of Cover while 12” away at least, now every ADEPTUS ASTARTES unit in your army has Stealth by default. 

DETACHMENT RULES

SHADOW TACTICS

The Raven Guard are renowned for their uncanny ability to move unseen, cloaking themselves in darkness as they close in upon their prey. Aethon Shaan is a true master at harnessing these abilities, withdrawing and redeploying his battle-brothers to draw the enemy out of formation.

Friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES units have Stealth. Friendly PHOBOS/SCOUT SQUAD units have -3" detection range.

Friendly AETHON SHAAN units have the following ability:

Unparalleled Tactician: (Once per battle round, per army) When you use the Into Darkness stratagem, that use is -1CP.

On top of that, PHOBOS and SCOUT units get -3” to their detection range, while Chapter Master all-star Aethon Shaan can still zoop up into Strategic Reserves for free once per battle round. 

The new Suppressed Weapons stratagem is a great way to take advantage of your hidden troops, as one INFANTRY unit can open up with their full firepower and yet remain safely hidden from return fire. They don’t even need to be part of the Phobos gang, so throw it on Eradicators with Heavy Bolters if you really want to and hose a big swarm from across the map.

SUPPRESSED WEAPONS (1CP)

SHADOWMARK TALON STRATAGEM

The Raven Guard commonly utilise integral suppressors, flash-hiders and other technology to dampen weapon reports and conceal muzzle flare, enabling battle-brothers to fire on unsuspecting foes without giving away their positions.

WHEN: Your Shooting phase, when a friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES INFANTRY unit has shot.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES INFANTRY unit. 

EFFECT: Those attacks do not prevent your unit from being hidden.

In addition to these two, the Ultramarines, Iron Hands, Imperial Fists and White Scars will also be getting updates to their special detachments.* Each features four enhancements and six stratagems, so you’ll have a mighty toolbox at your fingertips, and the detachments for the Iron Hands, Imperial Fists and White Scars are 2DP, opening up all sorts of options when you combine them with one of the many 1DP detachments from the Codex.

What ideas will you come up with? Shadowmark Talon and Phobos Shadow Force make your vanguard troops extra sneaky and hard to draw a bead on, while the Imperial Fists’ Ceramite Sentinels detachment is practically tailor-made to pair with Gravis Siege Force to create a legendary defensive line.

See the full spread of extra detachments in the Warhammer 40,000 app when Codex: Space Marines releases. It’s up for pre-order on Saturday, so it won’t be long now!

* An earlier version of this article said that White Scars weren't getting their own detachment. In a lightning manoeuvre typical of the sons of the Khan, one has just dropped into our inbox. White Scars players will be getting the Spearpoint Task Force for 2 DP.

https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.title: Miniatures Showcase – Cargo-8 Conversions
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.description: Get ready to head out on the Ash Road with these incredible Ridgehaulers.
https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-g.content_html:
We’re a few weeks into the new edition of Necromunda and our friends in the Warhammer Design Studio have been hard at work converting some suitable vehicles for their gangs.

Lucy

For my Cargo-8 Ridgehauler I really wanted the whole piece to feel ramshackle and upcycled. This crew roam the ash wastes looking for the next prize to chop up and sell to the highest bidder. Times are tough in the underhive though, and the crew have had to modify their vehicle on the fly using scraps and spares meant for sale just to keep this rig rolling!

You’ll see they’re transporting the remains of an Arvus Lighter and the front of the rig features the drilldozer from the front of a Goliath Rockgrinder.

Graham

After reading Spire of Primus, I was inspired by a piece of art which had an Enforcer patrol with two Ironcrawlers with cages on their back. I took this idea and developed it into what an armoured version for transporting VIPs (very important prisoners) would look like. I modified the Munitorum Armoured Container to look more like the back of a contemporary police van by adding barred windows and seating for those who have been deemed unworthy in the eyes of the Pax Helmawr. The main cab was slightly altered to fit the armour of the Enforcers and their trusty Cyber-mastiff (who takes pride of place by sticking their head out of the window).

The whole vehicle was then painted in the same colour scheme of my Enforcers while making the container slightly darker to give the feeling of a much older piece of equipment which has been in service for many years. The last job was to add a smattering of dirt and ash to the lower half of the vehicle, where dirt would naturally develop and build up after a long drive through the ash wastes.

Paul

The Cargo-8 Ridgehauler is such a great kit that I didn't really feel the need to convert it, I simply wanted to paint lots of them! Luckily the kit allows you to add up to four trailers. I had one goal I wanted to achieve – to make the Ridgehaulers appear a little heavier and sit deeper into the ground. Tyres on large heavy vehicles bulge and flatten out where they contact the ground, so my goal would prove to be an epic task as it involved sanding flat the tread of 32 wheels and making sure every wheel was the same height.

Dean

When the Cargo-8 challenge was suggested, I pulled one of those nagging projects from the back of my mind – Guild of Coin leased heavy industry vehicles. When I’d said the idea out loud, I had to follow through with it! Luckily, the old Galvanic Servohaulers had been made available on a Made To Order, so I grabbed a set and started work.

The truck cabs were enclosed with plasticard and wire mesh to give the models a heavier look. This enabled me to save the crew to use in the future to make the workers and guards to go along with the vehicles. The vehicles were sprayed with Leadbelcher, and then a rough red/brown layer was applied to the panel areas, followed by yellow applied via stippling to create a worn, and chipped look, emphasised by some added silver sponge chipping. An Agrax Earthshade wash was then applied to tint and unify the whole model, followed by more washes applied in streaks to emphasise that worn look.

These were intended to be used as terrain pieces on ash waste setups, but there is a very good chance I’m going to be making more, along with the workers and guards I mentioned. Now the new edition of Necromunda is here, maybe it’s time to make a new gang – perhaps a Guild of Coin-sponsored Outcast gang…

Thanks, folks! All of Ridgehaulers look ripe for a heist – we recommend some Orlock Outrider Quads to launch a speedy raid and quickly escape with your stolen swag.

Space Wolves

There’s a lot to get through today, so we’re going to make like Phobos-armoured marines and move 33% faster than before. Space Wolves get most of the same boosts as general Space Marine units, such as the extra point of Toughness on many datasheets – including Bjorn the Fell-handed – and have some unit abilities tweaked to work better with the new Space Marine paradigm.

Grey Hunters, for instance, have re-learned how to work in 5-man teams.

Grey Hunters must be taken in a squad of 10 as before, but now you can split them up into two 5-man units before deployment. This can help you cover much more ground and will give Space Wolves armies an edge in action-heavy missions.

Detachment-wise, the Space Wolves see Saga of the Beastslayer and Saga of the Great Wolf come back with minor tweaks – at 1DP and 2DP respectively – while the Champions of Fenris detachment takes a far more aggressive stance and replaces all three of its Stratagems with new, more deadly options.

TARGET: That ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit. 

EFFECT: Attacks that target your unit have -1 D until that enemy unit has attacked.

Otherwise, the units you know and love are still fighting fit after these changes, and you can combine the detachments here with any from the Space Marines Codex. 

Black Templars

The Black Templars have much more of a mix-up with their rules, as the three detachments they get in this update – Fist of the God-Emperor, Vow-sworn Crusaders, and Marshal’s Household – are all either changed or new. While the army previously had their own army rule in place of Oath of Moment, now they adhere to the new Combat Doctrines rule while the swearing of Templar Vows has been moved to the Vow-sworn Crusaders detachment.

DETACHMENT RULES

TEMPLAR VOWS

On the eve of battle, the Black Templars gather to be led in prayer and contemplation by their champions. United in their hatred of the foe, they swear a mighty vow to uphold in the battle ahead.

At the start of the first battle round, you can select one Vow listed below. That Vow is active for friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES units until the end of the battle.

ABHOR THE WITCH, DESTROY THE WITCH

  • Have [PRECISION].

  • Have [LANCE]. 

ACCEPT ANY CHALLENGE, NO MATTER THE ODDS

Friendly melee attacks that target a unit with a T greater than this unit’s S have +1 to wound rolls.

UPHOLD THE HONOUR OF THE EMPEROR

Friendly INFANTRY units have:

  • At the end of your Movement phase, if this unit is controlling an objective, that objective is secured.

  • When this unit is selected to make an advance move, that advance move does not prevent this unit from being eligible to start an action.

Restrictions: Your army can include BLACK TEMPLARS units, but it cannot include any ADEPTUS ASTARTES units drawn from any other Chapter.

As it costs only 2DP, Vow-sworn Crusaders fits nicely with plenty of the 1DP detachments kicking around in the new Codex, so if you want to Accept Any Challenge, No Matter the Odds and double down on close combat carnage with the Assault Brethren, you can.

Getting access to the Assault Doctrine’s ability to advance and charge is great news for the Emperor’s Champion, whose slimmed-down Sigismund’s Heir ability now gives a lovely +1 to charge rolls and doesn’t require them to end up engaged with a Character. Black Templars fans may lament the loss of the ability to give him Devastating Wounds once per battle, but don’t worry – it’s just baked right into the Black Sword’s Strike profile now.

The new Fist of the God-Emperor detachment, meanwhile, takes the part of the old Vindication Task Force ability that lets Crusader Squads make surge moves towards objectives and pairs it with stratagems and enhancements that directly boost the Black Templars’ iconic infantry squad. Giving big squads the Righteous Fervour upgrade will make them excellent objective-holders as they power towards the centre of the battlefield, safe in the knowledge that a few dead Neophytes only makes them get to their target quicker.

ENHANCEMENTS

With their zealous hatred stoked red-hot by furious sermons and inflammatory prayers, Companions of Vehemence are filled with a wrathful vigour. Only the deaths of the God-Emperor’s enemies can assuage their fury, and they will let nothing delay them from unleashing it.

Deathwatch

Finally, the Deathwatch get an update to their classic 3DP Black Spear Task Force detachment that ties their Mission Tactics to Combat Doctrines and gently upgrades a few of their stratagems, but the real party piece is the new 1DP Deathwatch Support detachment that uses the same detachment rule as the Black Spear Task Force, but allows a 500 point force of Deathwatch to be taken in any Space Marines army.

DETACHMENT RULES

MISSION TACTICS

Thousands of years of collated strategic data and hard-won combat experience have provided the Deathwatch with the ultimate battlefield tactics to combat almost any foe.

FUROR TACTICS 

When the enemy horde grows close, the Deathwatch will be tasked with the decimation of their core. Aiming not for clinical kills but for maximum destruction over a wide area, they tear the heart from the enemy army.

MALLEUS TACTICS 

When the giants of war lumber forth, the Deathwatch will adopt Malleus tactics. Even the largest behemoth has a weak point, and the archives of the Deathwatch number them all.

PURGATUS TACTICS 

By adopting Purgatus tactics, the Deathwatch focus their deadly ire upon the commanders of the enemy host, assassinating them one after another with pitiless head shots and killing thrusts of the blade.

Friendly KILL TEAM units with this ability have the following abilities:

Furor Tactics: If the devastator doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks have [SUSTAINED HITS 1].

Malleus Tactics: If the tactical doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks have [LETHAL HITS]. 

Purgatus Tactics: If the assault doctrine is active for your unit, your unit’s attacks that target an enemy unit within 9" of this unit have [PRECISION].

If you’ve ever wanted a team of elite veterans to hunt xenos prey while the rest of your army fights on the front line, this is the best way to do it. You can even give your best squad the ability to Deep Strike with the classic Beacon Angelis enhancement – provided they have a Character leading them – so if all you want is a single scary Kill Team ruining your opponent’s back line, you can do it.

All of these new rules will go live on the Warhammer 40,000 app when Codex: Space Marines releases, and with pre-orders happening this very weekend, you won’t have long to wait.

Neave Blacktalon and her companions are back in a new novel from Black Library, and they must face an enemy that even they may not be able to defeat.

In Shadow of the Silver Wolf by Gary Kloster, Neave travels to Greybank, a mysterious city wrapped in fog and nightmares. Here the Blacktalons must call on the experience they have gained in centuries of service to Sigmar. These are warriors who have lived and died countless times, willingly paying the price of their service with blood, pain and the pasts that have made them who they are today.*

In Greybank, their past comes back for them, and the Blacktalons must answer an almost impossible question – how do you fight a memory? Even with lifetimes of martial skill, and the best weapons the Mortal Realms can offer, how do you defeat despair?

Neave must find a way to do so, and discover the source of the curse that has twisted the city and its people, before her friendships, her loyalties, and her faith are torn apart.

Neave Blacktalon has also appeared in the Black Library novels, Blacktalon: First Mark by Andy Clark – where she hunted down a Tzeentchian wizard in the jungles north of Hammerhal Aqsha – and Blacktalon by Liane Merciel, where she faced five champions of Chaos who were seeking a long-buried, devastating weapon.**

Shadow of the Silver Wolf will be available to pre-order soon. In the meantime, dive into the Mortal Realms in one of Gary’s other Warhammer Age of Sigmar novels – Skaventide or Queen of the Rose Throne.

* Learn more about Neave’s past in the Warhammer TV animation Blacktalon.

The upcoming release of Codex: Space Marines heralds significant changes for almost every part of the faction, from datasheets to detachments. This also has a knock-on effect on other Space Marine factions that rely on those core rules, so over the next couple of days, we’re going to see how less Codex-compliant Chapters are being updated – starting with the Blood Angels and Dark Angels.

Blood Angels

When Codex: Space Marines releases, the Blood Angels, Dark Angels, Space Wolves, Black Templars, and Deathwatch will all get an overhaul of their units and detachments in the Warhammer 40,000 app, while the more Codex-compliant Chapters like the Salamanders and Imperial Fists will get updates to their specialist detachments. 

The Blood Angels, for instance, get a new 2DP version of Angelic Inheritors that focuses their detachment rule on the ability to re-roll 1s for Hit and Wound rolls (that everybody chose anyway) while still offering four enhancements and six stratagems with plenty of familiar favourites. Their new Measured Strategist stratagem is a versatile tool that lets a unit slip into whichever Combat Doctrine they please, so even if most of your army fancies having Assault on their guns, Dante and his Sanguinary Guard can advance and charge right into the thick of it.

MEASURED STRATEGIST (1CP)

ANGELIC INHERITORS STRATAGEM

Stern and level-headed, this Blood Angels commander is a beacon of composure amidst the tempest of his brothers’ fury, providing much-needed tactical guidance for his impetuous battle-brothers. 

WHEN: Your Command phase.

TARGET: One friendly ADEPTUS ASTARTES CHARACTER unit. 

EFFECT: Select one combat doctrine. That combat doctrine is active for your unit until the start of your next Command phase.

As true sons of Sanguinius will know, Angelic Inheritors specifically affects CHARACTER units – whether they’re running around on their own or leading their subordinates – and they’re getting a few upgrades of their own. Commander Dante now activates the Assault and Tactical doctrines for his unit at all times, while everyone’s favourite Black Rage survivor Mephiston is stronger, tougher, and faster than ever.

Dark Angels

Over on the Dark Angels side of the aisle, their Wrath of the Rock detachment also returns at 2DP, primed for being combined with the wide assortment of 1DP detachments in Codex: Space Marines. 

Most of their enhancements and stratagems are the classics you know and love, but Armour of Contempt and Leonine Aggression* get swapped out for In Sacrifice, Victory and Knights of Iron. The former lets a Deathwing or Ravenwing unit secure an objective with their dying breath, while the latter sends skilled Ravenwing pilots and riders buzzing around seemingly solid terrain with the MOBILE keyword.

Those inducted into the Dark Angels’ Inner Circle will gladly give their lives in pursuit of victory, and to see the Fallen brought to justice.

That objective is secured.

Pre-orders for Codex: Space Marines are less than a week away, but there’s still plenty of time to have a look inside at the new rules. Today, we’re showing off some awesome new datasheets – including the Avenging Son himself.

As the author of the Codex Astartes, it should come as no surprise that Roboute Guilliman can use all of its tenets as easily as breathing, manifesting as him having all parts of the new Combat Doctrines army rule active at all times. Not only does this mean that he can Advance, Fall Back, Shoot, and Charge at will, whenever he likes, but it also interacts with a few stratagems from the new detachments to boost their effects.

He can also bestow a Combat Doctrine of his choice on a nearby ally, and unlike other sources of alternative doctrines, this one is active alongside any others you picked for the turn. Between this and his new Primarch of the XIII aura, which more directly enhances the hitting power of everyone around him, he’s a superb support character who just happens to also be great at punching heretics’ heads clean off.

As you may have seen from the rules in Codex: Orks, Psykers now have a psyker level that determines how many powers they can use in a turn. This wouldn’t be much use if everyone just had the one, so now Librarians of all stripes have different powers they can activate – like the regular Librarian’s Veil of Time and Force Dome options.

You don’t always need that (undoubtedly handy) 4+ Invulnerable Save, especially in the later stages of the game when dashing to objectives is vital, so now a quick Veil of Time will maximise your Advances instead. Librarians in Phobos armour can shroud their unit with a -1 To Hit ward or strip the cover from their unit’s target, while those in Terminator armour can boost the strength of their melee attacks or the range of their guns.

Speaking of guns, the undisputed marksmanship masters of the First Company, the Sternguard Veterans, now have a vastly expanded selection of shooting profiles they can use.*

Their new artificer firearms encompass all kinds of special boltguns, combi-weapons, and ammunition their models are equipped with, and give them a choice of weapon types to emulate every time they open fire. When attacking an enemy Vehicle, they can pick Damnatus to get the high Strength, AP, and Damage of a meltagun, while Infernus loads up the newly improved stats of a bolt rifle and adds Rapid Fire 2 for extra carnage.

We could hardly finish things up without showing off Terminators, especially after we talked about their snazzy new detachment last week, and they don’t disappoint with better Toughness, better bolters, and a new Hunter profile** on their chainfists to put the fear of the Emperor into Vehicles and Monsters.

Their new take on Fury of the First makes cracking armour a breeze when you’re face-to-face with the foe, and it works all the time – even in close combat. If you add in the improved assault cannon stat line, you’re getting an AP -3, Sustained Hits 1 death machine that can chop up almost anything man-sized with little effort.

That’s just a little taste of how some of the datasheets have changed in the new Codex. Come back tomorrow as we start looking at rules updates for less Codex-compliant Chapters, starting with the Blood Angels and Dark Angels.

* Superficially similar to Flash Gitz and Killa Kans, but don’t tell them that.
** We took a first look at Hunter when we first showed off the new datasheet for the Tankbusters.

The ground is shaking, the boulders are flying, and the Sons of Behemat are lumbering towards their next big scrap. Today, Anthony Magro from AoS Coach reveals the new battletome builds that could bring the biggest smash to the battlefield. 

Anthony:  The last time I wrote about the Sons of Behemat for Warhammer Community was back in 2021, when the army’s game plan was reasonably straightforward – put an enormous Mega-Gargant on an objective and ask your opponent what they planned to do about it. 

They may still prefer to settle arguments by throwing their weight around, but the new Battletome: Sons of Behemat gives them many more options than simply marching forwards and hoping something breaks.

The Sons’ defining strengths remain: gargants are enormous, hard-hitting monsters with devastating charges and enough battlefield presence to demand an immediate response. But the new battletome gives them more tools, from Ma Maegran, Boss-stompers, and Rock-hurlers to specialised units that seize objectives, bombard the enemy, screen vulnerable areas, and create openings for a gargant to strike. They still solve problems with brute force, but now they have more say in which problem gets flattened first. That opens the door to combat-focused forces, ranged armies, specialised-unit builds, and devastating all-out assaults led by Kragnos. 

Here are three mighty gatherings of gargants that could leave an unforgettable mark on the Mortal Realms. 

Sons of Behemat – 1970/2000 pts 
Battle Formation: Looting Leviathans 
Spell Lore: Lore of Behemat 
Prayer Lore: Lore of the World Titan 
Manifestation Lore: Primal Energy
Battle Tactics: Burning for Vengeance, Legend of the Parch 

General’s Regiment 
King Brodd (430) 
• General
Kraken-eater Mega-Gargant (370)
• Artefacts of Power: Krakenskin Sandals (10) 

Regiment 1
Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant (380)
• Heroic Trait:  Unreasonable Tyrant (0)
• Realm-Shaking Rampage: Earthshaking Roar (20)
Warstomper Mega-Gargant (390)
Boss-stompers (370) 

The Boss-stompers might be LITTLE by Sons of Behemat standards, but there's nothing little about what happens when three of them reach combat. This army is built around getting them there, then having the bigger gargants pile into the same fight and make an already dangerous unit considerably nastier. 

The Beast-smasher is their natural partner. Rather than simply being another Mega-Gargant sent off to smash things by itself, I want it fighting alongside the Boss-stompers. I'll often build the Beast-smasher towards STRIKE-FIRST using the army's battle traits, allowing it to swing before the Boss-stompers and use Leader of the Pack to give their melee weapons Crit (2 Hits). Earthshaking Roar can also stop the unfortunate target from using commands, which is particularly useful when you don't want All-out Defence taking some of the sting out of what's coming next. 

Looting Leviathans is my preferred battle formation for this version of the army, because once the Boss-stompers make their charge I want them getting to the thing that actually matters. Argy Bargy can add 3" to their pile-in moves for the rest of the turn, giving them a 6" pile-in, while Get to the Goods lets a charging BIG or LITTLE unit pass across enemy models in non-MONSTER units while doing so. A screen that looked perfectly sensible at the start of the Charge phase can suddenly become much less reassuring. 

LOOTING LEVIATHANS

Passive

GET TO THE GOODS

When shiny treasure or barrels of grog are sighted, these gargants wade through ranks of little 'uns without pause.

Effect: Each time a friendly BIG or LITTLE unit that charged in the same turn makes a pile-in move, that unit can pass across enemy models in non-MONSTER units.

The rest of the army helps make that engagement happen. The Warstomper can move another BIG or LITTLE unit 2D6" in the Movement phase, while the Kraken-eater and the Beast-smasher's Unreasonable Tyrant heroic trait can each add 1 to the Boss-stompers' charge roll. King Brodd can then add 1 to the Rend of their melee weapons with Power of Behemat prayer, while remaining a serious threat in his own right. 

There's even a nasty reversal if your opponent decides to charge the Boss-stompers first. Quit Hogging Da Fun! lets them bring a nearby BIG unit into the fight immediately after they attack in the enemy combat phase. On my turn, the Beast-smasher sets up the Boss-stompers. On yours, the Boss-stompers can drag one of the big lads into the punch-up with them. 

I've deliberately taken four different Mega-Gargants here to maximise their different Once Per Turn (Army) abilities, but there is another way to build the same idea. If I swapped King Brodd for Ma Maegran, I would also replace the Warstomper with a second unit of Boss-stompers. That redundancy matters because Chooser of the Mighty can sacrifice a LITTLE model to return a destroyed non-UNIQUE BIG unit, and I don't want to weaken my only Boss-Stomper unit just to bring a Mega-Gargant back. 

Either way, the plan is wonderfully straightforward – get the gang together, pick the biggest problem on the battlefield, and introduce it to an unreasonable number of clubs. 

Sons of Behemat – 1990/2000 pts 
Battle Formation: Heirs of the Old Ways 
Spell Lore: Lore of Behemat 
Prayer Lore: Brodd’s Bellows (Scourge of Aqshy) 
Manifestation Lore: Primal Energy 
Battle Tactics: Blazing Onslaught, Burning for Vengeance 

General’s Regiment 
Ma Maegran (370) 
• General 
Ancient Ghyrochs (0) 
Boss-stompers (370) 

Regiment 1 
King Brodd (430) 
Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant (400) 
• Heroic Trait:  Always First In (0) 
• Artefacts of Power: Glowy Lantern (20) 
• Realm-Shaking Rampage: Earthshaking Roar (20) 
Rock-hurlers (380) 

Sons of Behemat armies have never exactly been famous for subtle ranged warfare, but the new Rock-hurlers give you a very different way to approach the battlefield. Rather than racing everything into combat, this army wants to apply pressure from range, force the opponent to come towards you, and then let King Brodd and the Boss-stompers finish whatever survives the opening bombardment. 

The Gatebreaker is what makes that shooting package really work. Rip It Up and Chuck It lets it uproot nearby terrain and improve the Rock-hurlers' or its own shooting, giving each Rock-hurler model an extra attack with its ranged weapons. The Rock-hurlers can then adapt with Drop, Toss or Roll depending on what the turn demands with extra range when the target is keeping its distance, better accuracy when you need the damage, or Shoot in Combat when somebody inevitably decides charging the gargants will solve the problem. 

Ma Maegran fits beautifully behind that firing line. While she stays close to another Sons of Behemat Monster, The Wandering Witch makes her invisible to enemies more than 12" away, allowing her to sit behind the Gatebreaker and Rock-hurlers and concentrate on supporting the army rather than worrying about being picked off. I generally keep the Ancient Ghyrochs nearby too, using Shepherdess to increase Ma's power level and give me more magical options each turn. 

This is also where I really like bringing the Scourge of Aqshy season rules into the army. King Brodd is already a Priest, and the Glowy Lantern lets me make the Gatebreaker another one. That gives me two sources of the Rock Bottom prayer,* which grants a 6+ Ward and lets a unit ignore the effects of Battle Damaged. For an army built around several expensive gargants, keeping a wounded Mega-Gargant operating at full effectiveness while the opponent tries to weather the shooting can be enormously valuable. 

TITANIC TROPHIES

Deployment Phase

GLOWY LANTERN

Stolen from the aelves of Hysh after a botched alliance, this aetherquartz jar was at first carried around just because it was shiny. Over time, it has granted its bearer an innate power.

Effect: If this unit is a WIZARD or PRIEST, add 1 to its power level for the rest of the battle. Otherwise, pick either the WIZARD (1) or PRIEST (1) keyword. This unit has that keyword for the rest of the battle.

Heirs of the Old Ways is my preferred battle formation here. This list wants its firing lanes and support pieces operating cleanly, so being able to interfere with enemy Wizards or Priests and potentially clear away the manifestations they have summoned helps stop the army from being pinned down before it can dictate the engagement. 

Once the enemy does close the distance, that is where Brodd and the Boss-stompers take over. The shooting does not necessarily have to destroy the target outright – it just has to make the fight that follows unfair in your favour. 

You could double down and replace the Boss-stompers with another unit of Rock-hurlers, or trade them for three individual Mancrushers to gain more scoring pieces and cleaner sacrifices for Chooser of the Mighty. If you do take three Mancrushers, it is also worth considering the Hammer Throw Realm-shaking Rampage, which lets you throw a Mancrusher 3D6" and potentially launch it straight into combat. I prefer the mixed version, though. Your opponent can stay back and get rocks thrown at them, or come closer and discover that the ammunition was never the biggest threat. 

Sons of Behemat – 1960/2000 pts 
Battle Formation: Looting Leviathans 
Spell Lore: Lore of Behemat 
Prayer Lore: Lord of the World Titan 
Manifestation Lore: Aetherwrought Machineries 
Battle Tactics: Burning for Vengeance, Legend of the Parch 

General’s Regiment 
Kragnos (580) 
• General 
Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant (380) 
• Heroic Trait:  Brute of Brutes (0) 
• Artefacts of Power: Glowy Lantern (20) 
• Realm-Shaking Rampage: Earthshaking Roar (20) 

Regiment 1 
King Brodd (430) 
Scourge of Aqshy Mancrusher (150) 
• Cracked Heels: That Boy’s Not Right (10) 

Regiment 2 
Ma Maegran (370) 
Ancient Ghyrochs (0) 

Sometimes the best way to control the battlefield is to make sure your opponent never gets comfortable on it. This list is built around Kragnos doing exactly that, using his 3D6” charge support to turn the opening turns into an immediate threat while the rest of the army piles in behind him. 

King Brodd is a big part of making that happen. Through World Titan’s Stride, he can add 3" to Kragnos’ Move and let him pass across enemy models and terrain as though he had FLY. Kragnos already threatens an enormous distance thanks to those 3D6” charges, so giving him even more freedom to move around screens or awkward terrain helps make sure he reaches the fight you actually care about rather than the one your opponent wants to offer you. 

Once he gets there, the Beast-smasher and Ma Maegran start layering on the support. Leader of the Pack can give Kragnos Crit (2 Hits), while Creepy Cantrips can add 1 to hit rolls for his combat attacks. Brodd can then contribute Power of Behemat for extra Rend. I don’t need every one of those effects every turn, but having access to them means Kragnos can go from being a fast hammer to an absolutely brutal one when the right target presents itself.

MA MAEGRAN

CHOOSER OF THE MIGHTY

Your Hero Phase

CREEPY CANTRIPS

Maegran has memorised many weird, witchy cantrips and mutter-curses. If performed with enough gusto and allied to her sinister reputation, the resulting sense of menace can goad nearby gargants into terrified action.

Declare: Pick a visible friendly SONS OF BEHEMAT MONSTER unit wholly within 18" of this unit to be the target, then make a casting roll of 2D6.

Effect: Until the start of your next turn, add 1 to rampage rolls for the target and add 1 to hit rolls for the target's combat attacks.

The Beast-smasher carries the Glowy Lantern and Earthshaking Roar, giving me another Priest and a way to switch off commands on whatever I’m trying to overwhelm. Brute of Brutes helps keep its own attacks reliable, which matters because I don’t want it to be standing around as a passive support piece – it should be arriving in the same combat and helping Kragnos finish the job. 

Ma Maegran fills a different role here to the previous list. I’m less interested in hiding her behind a shooting castle and more interested in having her follow the main assault as a mobile magical support piece. The Ancient Ghyrochs help increase her power level, giving her the casting bandwidth to keep feeding useful buffs into the front line. 

The Scourge of Aqshy Mancrusher is the cheap utility piece that makes the list tick. It can contribute to mission play, dabble in prayers through That Boy’s Not Right, and since it has the LITTLE keyword it becomes an ideal sacrifice for Chooser of the Mighty if the Beast-smasher goes down. That means I can afford to throw the Beast-smasher into dangerous combats knowing Ma may be able to bring it back later. 

This isn’t the subtle Sons list. It’s the one that wants to seize the initiative, hit first, and make the opponent start solving problems immediately. 

If Kragnos is known as the End of Empires, this army is really just trying to make sure he gets started early. 

More Than A One-Hit Wonder 

These three lists only scratch the surface of what the new Sons of Behemat battletome can do. 

You can double down on Rock-hurlers and turn the army into a much heavier ranged threat, build around multiple Boss-stomper units for redundancy, lean harder into Mancrushers for mission play, or explore very different combinations of Mega-Gargants depending on which support abilities you value most. Ma Maegran alone opens up a whole range of list-building decisions around magic, LITTLE units and bringing destroyed Mega-Gargants back into the fight. 

That is probably what I like most about this battletome. There is no longer one obvious question of which Mega-Gargants hit hardest. Instead, I find myself asking which gargants I want working together, what role each one is filling, and how those pieces help the army control the battlefield. 

The Sons of Behemat are still enormous, still destructive, and still perfectly capable of solving problems by hitting them with something the size of a building. They just have a few more ways to decide which building to use. 

Thanks, Anthony! Grab the new Sons of Behemat battletome, along with Ma Maegran, and the Boss-stompers/Rock-hurlers kit, when it goes on sale tomorrow.

The new Sons of Behemat miniatures and battletome are available for pre-order tomorrow! Get ready for the latest stomp with a free piece of Warhammer Age of Sigmar fiction.

King Brodd does not often dream. When he does, he dreams of the lightning.

Which is not really a surprise. He has seen plenty of lightning, raging on the horizon or being hurled by some squawking little ’un. But only one instance – one irreversible moment – is the lightning. You don’t readily forget a display of such absolute power that it burns out your eye and murders a god.

Especially when that god is your father.

But Brodd, when he bothers to acknowledge his dreams at all, reminds himself to keep quiet. There are certain things a king doesn’t talk about. There are also certain things that a proper gargant doesn’t talk about.

So, when he tells the tales to audiences of rapt, gawping gargants, Brodd doesn’t mention the lightning that crackles through his sparse dreams, though he proclaims what he intends to do to the storm-godling of Azyr viscerally and often. He describes in punishing detail how he’ll twist the Sigmar the Hammer King’s limbs off and squash him between huge, wart-encrusted toes, but he never mentions the scar in his mind’s eye. He recounts seeing Behemat, the World Titan, topple into death as Sigmar’s treacherous bolts struck him, but he says nothing of the feeling that welled in his own chest as he did so. 

Any gargant who tries to delve deeper with questions gets a scowl and a cuff round the head, at best. Brodd tells them the stories, but it is not his job to bare his soul to them. His task is vengeance – and vengeance alone.

Yet now there’s another breed of lightning, and this one does not haunt his sleep. It’s real. It crackles an evil green as it comes closer, dripping from the rusty iron fangs of the vermin-machine forcing him into the slop of the Scabrous Sprawl. Cold mud crawls up Brodd’s leg as he pushes back against that mechanised pressure. 

‘Come on,’ the lightning seems to say, ‘sleep where Behemat slept. Die where your father died.’ 

In answer, Brodd roars. Spittle flies from gaps in his teeth onto the Parasite Engine he’s wrestling with – a huge, skittering, multi-limbed mechanical monster. Ratmen swarm over the machine’s hide of scrap, adding their shrill voices to the cacophony. Brodd grits his teeth and strains at the metal limbs, bunching every muscle. His eye feels like it’s going to pop. He tries to summon up the divine strength of his forefather, but he finds it won’t come. He grunts, demanding it, and still it won’t come.

The sounds of other gargants battling against the tide of gnashing, slashing rats has grown distant. He wonders what he looks like to them. Strong? Like a king, with his veins bulging and nostrils flaring? It doesn’t matter. The Engine’s mouth is getting closer, jaws grinding open and spitting electrical hate. He might die.

And it’ll be the lightning that kills him.

‘Did ye dream last eve, Brodd of the Behemati?’

It’s Maegran who says it. The Chooser of the Mighty waits until dark has fallen and the campfire, made of three trees stacked atop one another, has burned to cold embers. Her wind-crackle voice stirs Brodd just as he was beginning to nod off. The other gargants of the war party are already asleep, their snores rumbling like the echo of some cosmic birth.

‘What?’

‘Did ye dream?’ Maegran stands at the edge of the camp, leaning on her spear and smoking a pipe carved from some ancient, mouldy bone. For all her apparent age and creaking limbs, the wyrdy-witch of the bogs has yet to actually sit down in all the time Brodd has known her. Right now, that is only about two days, but it still strikes him as off. One of her moss-furred brutes snuffles around at her feet. Maegran grasps the torc clasped around its neck and gives it a yank that is possibly meant to be affectionate.

‘No,’ Brodd lies. Unconsciously, his hand finds his great obelisk-club, patting it.

‘Liar.’ Maegran chortles and blows a smoke-ring that shimmers off into the night. When she looks back at him, there’s a snaggle-tooth sneer about her. 

‘All the kings what was dreamed. When we ruled these lands and the little ’uns knelt to us, our kings dreamed.’

‘Good fer them.’

‘That ain’t kingly, Brodd.’ She’s still smirking. It makes Brodd scowl. 

‘What’d you know about that?’

‘Told you. I spoke to ’em. The old Behemati kings. Back before there was storm gods and spiky gods; when there was real gargants to be king of.’

‘What’re we, then?’

‘You’re the boss. You tell me.’

This cyclical, riddling sort of talk that Maegran so enjoys makes Brodd’s head hurt. There’s a gabbling hiss by his left ear. One of the red-fleshed imps that always cling to him apparently has an opinion. Brodd pushes the Creeper down with a finger; it flees just in time to avoid being squashed.

Brodd’s knees protest as he stands. He steps through the mass of sleeping gargants, reminding himself with some effort not to simply stomp on his own subjects. A few sleep close to where Maegran lurks: her followers, who think her magics can make them mighty if she chooses. To Brodd, it seems stupid at best, vaguely blasphemous at worst. In the future, it might be a problem. But for now – ‘now’ being the long and vengeful present that will persist until Sigmar is bloody paste, which is all that really matters to Brodd – she is an ally. 

‘You didn’t talk to no kings of old, witch,’ Brodd says as he stomps to the edge of the clearing and stares over the marshy, misty flats below. ‘All just tales on your part.’ 

Far out in the night’s gloom, amongst the mists of the Scabrous Sprawl, light sparks a faint green. If what Maegran told him in her cave was true, then there are ratmen in the deep swamps. They seek to scavenge weapons that Brodd smashed up when they disturbed the World Titan’s slumber. Now they profane his very grave. But the Sprawl is gargant turf, hence the warband sleeping at Brodd’s back, ready to smash and bash when the light rises.

‘No?’ Maegran crows a cackle that sees several slumbering gargants grunt and turn over, landslides in miniature. ‘No wonder ye be a king! You know me better than I know myself. Even the World Titan might have rumbled approval at that.’

‘You didn’t know him, neither. I won’t hear that rot.’

‘Best hope that. Perhaps ye wouldn’t like to know what he’d have thought of all this. If he thought of you at all.’

‘What’s that, witch?’

‘Well, what’s the legend of Brodd, really? Smashing little after little in one long rage? And how often do ye think of all these oafs at yer side, battling and hanging on to your every word? What are your people in this grand stomp o’ vengeance?

It’s not the answer he expects. For a long few moments, Brodd – scowling, stomping, bellowing Brodd – doesn’t know what to say. He’s the Prophet, isn’t he? Empowered, haunted, by the scraps of their dead father’s spirit? He glances around at the sleeping mob: Odro with his perpetually drooling nose; the triplets Fog, Marog, and Babog, all slumped in a snoring heap and with the messy refuse of the humans they gobbled up smeared around their mouths; Begra, who grunts in approval at every word he says and stands beside him with arms folded like some enforcer, with that corposant scar on her gut she wears so proudly. Then he turns to Maegran, one good eye narrowed amongst his drake-skull helmet, distant lightning illuminating his face.

‘You’re a tester, Chooser of the Mighty.’

‘Is that not what I’m for, King of the Bigs? To keep all you lunks honest and worthy of yer blood?’ Maegran maintains that wry smile, but there is something off-putting in her gaze now. The many carven faces hung across her frame glare and speak not.

‘You’ve come back here, to where Behemat was shot down by those even stronger than he, to smash the rats with all that godly strength what clings to you, Brodd. And aye, that be right and proper. But bigness ain’t always just size. Sometimes, bigness be in spirit. There’ll be a moment where ye’ll have to reckon with that.’

He doesn’t like the sound of that.

‘Don’t like the sound of that.’

‘But ye’ll know it,’ Maegran says, and there’s a twinkle in her evil eye now. ‘And ye’d best be ready for it. Else ye’ll find yerself a king of naught but mud and weeds.’

For a while, Brodd forgets the conversation. It seems like meandering night-talk from the wyrdy-witch, which he’s already come to learn is par for the course. Besides, the start of next morning’s battle goes well. The mists of the Scabrous Sprawl pull in thick, as if intending to shield the gargants from view as they approach the sparks of green. Then they charge out of the murk with voices raised in hullabaloo, kicking through mobs of screaming ratmen and hurling rocks to send cannons exploding into brass scraps and splinters. 

And then, at the heart of the bog, some screeching rodent techno-warlock manages to spark enough lightning and pull enough levers to bring the Parasite Engine back to life. It rises from the mire, venting waves of poison gas. A spear of green lightning shoots out from some horn-like projector and burns through Begra’s throat. She topples backwards, a tidal wave of brackish water sploshing where she falls, and that’s it, dead, eyes dull with incomprehension as they stare skywards. Brodd is still thinking that that’s no way for a gargant to go as the Engine brings its terrible weight down towards him. He catches its clawing forelimbs just in time.

And then the lightning’s coming to kill him.

Just before the machine’s power can overwhelm him entirely, something sees it lurch with a great metallic screech. Slick, bloated vines have writhed their way out of the bog-water to wrap around one of its limbs, pulling hard enough that it loses balance. It grants reprieve, enough for Brodd to stagger back and get his footing. He hears Maegran muttering mystic chants over his shoulder, feels energy crackling off her levelled spear and off the snorting beasts at her side as she weaves her spell.

She’s saved him. It still might not matter. Those gargants who have followed him here are quivering, starting to break. Their king was almost overwhelmed. That, it seems, means something to them. The Parasite Engine regains its footing with a mechanical hiss, its armour panels flaking. Brodd can just about imagine the manic rat at its control, grinning in what it thinks is victory.

‘OI!’

Brodd roars the word like some artillery barrage. The battlefield falls still as that tectonic explosion of sound issues forth. Even the Parasite Engine seems to draw back, startled and wary. Brodd steps forward, beating his fist upon his scarred chest and snorting. Around him, the watching gargants begin to chant low and stomp their humungous feet. Normally, he finds it faintly annoying. Now, Brodd goes so far as to give a leering grin.

‘You come ’ere, rat, to gargant turf, and you think you can take what you want? Nah. Into the bogs with you lot. Down to rot and be forgotten, in the shadow of our father’s bones. As all pipsqueaks should.’

Every word is slow, and low, and clear, and mocking. It is, after a fashion, kingly. The Parasite Engine appears to take umbrage. Power crackles along its vanes and prongs once more as its mechanical rodent skull stares into Brodd’s unflinching gaze. 

Except King Brodd is already moving, faster than anything as immense as he should move. Strength rises in him again, the might of Behemat, flowing as his followers chant his name and stomp that rhythmic beat of power. Maegran’s spell-beckoned tendrils yank down on the Engine once more, pulling it further into the marsh. Its focus is broken just long enough for Brodd to take his club in a two-handed grip and swing it like a meteor.

The obelisk-club crashes into the Parasite Engine’s iron flesh and keeps going. It buckles metals and whirring motors to set off a chain of furious detonations within, gouts of warpflame incinerating wailing Skaven crew. Brodd rips its weapon out in a burst of machine guts. He lets it slam down, throwing up a torrent of filth-water. He has enough time to spit into the open jaws of the Engine before it is torn apart from within by explosions.

It takes him a moment to realise that the roar he hears isn’t only the machine bursting into flames. His gargants are chanting his name. They’ve done so many times before, but this instance feels different to Brodd. Or maybe he’s just actually listening to it for the first time. It’s the sort of thing he could get used to, if he let himself.

‘Now, there be a sight,’ Maegran says as she wades to Brodd’s side, watching with a murmur as the wreck of the Parasite Engine begins to sink into the marsh. ‘Maybe Behemat’d have looked at a thing like that.’

‘Hmm,’ Brodd grunts. ‘Kingly, were it?’

‘Oh, aye. It’s a start.’ Something in the way she says it makes Brodd chuckle, a sound strange even to him. He shakes off the last prickles of the blast and lifts his good eye. The Skaven salvagers are panicking, splashing to and fro through the waters of the Sprawl in an attempt to escape, and eager gargants are already barrelling off after them with long, ungainly strides. But some of the ratman chieftains are trying to pull them back into a semblance of order, lashing them with their tails and jabbing towards the titans with cruel spears.

‘Well, yer bigness,’ Maegran says, ‘looks like the job ain’t done yet.’

‘Good,’ Brodd says, gripping his mace in both hands once more. ‘This place belongs to the Behemati. And I’m just gettin’ warmed up.’

The new Brawlers of Behemat boxed set is available to pre-order from Saturday, so we’re taking a look at just how two mighty Mega-Gargants smashing each other works.

Brawlers of Behemat is the game of monstrous melee and bone-crunching combat for two players. You’ll both shatter limbs, hurl buildings, and try to pummel your opponent into submission, and games can last around 15 minutes – perfect for play in a lunch break or as a warm up for a game of Warhammer Age of Sigmar.

The Mega-Gargants in the box can each be built as a Warstomper, Kraken-eater, or Gatebreaker, who have different attacks and abilities. They each start with the Clobber attack, and as they take more damage, they get angrier, which gives them access to even more devastating attacks.

CLOBBER

Randomise a body part on the other brawler and inflict D6 damage on it. Then, move the other brawler up to 1 stride in any direction.

When you make the Clobber attack, you randomly strike a body part of your opposing Mega-Gargant – head, torso, right arm, left arm, right leg, or left leg. Cause enough damage to the head, torso, or any two limbs, and your foe is taken down!

Each body part has a tracker so you know how badly damaged it is. When the damage token advances to a different colour (from white to green, or green to orange), your battle fury increases and you gain access to bigger, more powerful events. For example, the Warstomper can perform the Kicked in the Goolies attack! 

RIGHT LEG (5)

KICKED IN THE GOOLIES

Inflict D6 damage on the other brawler’s torso. If you inflicted more than 4 damage, advance the other brawler’s battle fury tracker down 1 box (i.e. from white to green or green to orange).

You might also notice the red skull shield – these are a reaction space. When the damage token reaches one of these, your Mega-Gargant can use the special ability on their dashboard – the Kraken-eater gets to use Netted and get access to some handy re-rolls.

NETTED

In this brawler’s next turn, when rolling to see how much damage an attack inflicts, you can re-roll any or all of the dice from that roll.

When a brawler takes sufficient damage, they each get access to Colossal Smash. This attack damages each body part of your opponent AND does even more damage as you knock them through a terrain piece.

COLOSSAL SMASH

Place the other brawler within 1 stride of your brawler. If you wish to place the other brawler in a space occupied by any buildings or barricades, remove them before placing the brawler. Then inflict D6 damage on each of the other brawler’s body parts, starting with the torso. For each barricade and building removed, you can add 2 to one of those D6 rolls (say whether you will do so before making the roll).

This fun, fast-paced game is also a great way to kick off a new Sons of Behemat army or easily add a pair of Mega-Gargants to an existing one. Rules for King Brodd and the Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant will also be in a future issue of White Dwarf.

Brawlers of Behemat is available to pre-order from Saturday, alongside the new Sons of Behemat battletome and miniatures, so you don’t have long to wait until you can duel in the ruins of Embergard.

Armies of Renown are a great way to add some extra theming to your Warhammer Age of Sigmar armies and trade a little flexibility for fun and characterful rules. Today, we’re seeing what the Sons of Behemat have to offer.

The new gargant witch Ma Maegran can gather a gaggle of LITTLE* units into the Matriarch’s Mob – a roving entourage of attendants and true believers who hope to prove themselves and earn a blessing from the Chooser of the Mighty. Even those closest to her have no idea how far her powers truly flex, and many far-fetched stories that start with “I Heard She Can…” end up proving shockingly true.

MATRIARCH'S MOB

Once Per Turn (Army), Your Hero Phase

I’VE HEARD SHE CAN…

Ma Maegran's true abilities are shrouded in mystery, but rumours will always exist, and gargants are nothing if not susceptible to a good yarn.

Effect: Pick 1 of the following effects:

...Shoot Fire From Her Eyes!: Inflict D3 mortal damage on each visible enemy unit within 12" of the friendly Ma Maegran.

...Turn You Into a Human!: Pick a visible friendly unit wholly within 12" of the friendly Ma Maegran. Until the start of your next turn, enemy units have a maximum control score of 1 while they are in combat with that unit.

...Make Ya Big and Strong!: Pick another visible friendly unit wholly within 12" of the friendly Ma Maegran. Add 1 to the Attacks characteristic of that unit's weapons for the rest of the turn.

...Whiz the Biggest Bangers!: Add 1 to casting rolls for the friendly Ma Maegran until the start of your next turn.

Many of the battle traits, enhancements, and spells unique to this Army of Renown affect targets within 12” of Ma Maegran, so it works best as a close-knit wrecking ball that rumbles from one objective to the next. The witch is so vital to the game plan that many of her gargants will gladly throw themselves in front of harm, for fear of disappointing the Chooser and catching a curse that saps them of their strength. 

MATRIARCH'S MOB

Passive

DON’T LET NUFFIN’ HAPPEN TO HER!

Ma Maegran is a figure of veneration and no small amount of fear among gargantkind. Hoping to be made 'really, really big', most gargants will do everything they can to keep her alive.

Effect: While the friendly Ma Maegran is within the combat range of another friendly LITTLE unit:

  • She has WARD (5+).

  • Each time you make a successful ward roll for her, allocate 1 mortal damage to another friendly LITTLE unit within her combat range after the damage sequence for her has been resolved (ward rolls cannot be made for those damage points).

  • Ignore negative modifiers to hit rolls and wound rolls for that other friendly LITTLE unit's combat attacks.

The next Army of Renown, the Stomper Tribe,** also rewards keeping smaller gargants around a locus of power, though this time one of the towering Warstomper Mega-Gargants. With a name like that you can probably guess what their favourite activity is, and the battle trait Stomp! Stomp! Stomp! Stomp! is a very thematically appropriate way to pile mortal damage into your foes.

STOMPER TRIBE

Once Per Turn (Army), Any Combat Phase

STOMP! STOMP! STOMP! STOMP!

The Stomper Tribe are famous for one thing, and you'll never guess what it is...

Declare: Pick an enemy unit in combat with a friendly STOMPER TRIBE unit to be the target.

Effect: Roll a dice. Add 1 to the roll for each friendly STOMPER TRIBE model in combat with the target. On a 5+:

  • The target has STRIKE-LAST for the rest of the turn.

  • Inflict 3 mortal damage on the target.

Where the Matriarch’s Mob has loads of utility abilities that can heal friendly units, fortify their hides, or order them out of risky combats, the Stomper Tribe is all about killing squishy little mortals as much as you possibly can. The Gettin’ Stuck In ability is a flexible way to boost both your LITTLE horde and your BIG unit in combat, giving the melee weapons used by the former an extra point of Damage – upping their swings with their weapon to an impressive 3 Damage and their ‘Eadbutt to Damage 4 – while the latter’s melee weapons have more Rend to bust through pesky armour.

STOMPER TRIBE

Once Per Turn (Army), Any Combat Phase

GETTIN’ STUCK IN

Warstompers and their followers relish the visceral thrill of battle, wading in wherever the fighting is most bloody.

Declare: Pick a friendly STOMPER TRIBE unit in combat to be the target.

Effect: If the target is LITTLE, pick a model in the target unit. Add 1 to the Damage characteristic of that model's melee weapons for the rest of the turn.

If the target is BIG, add 1 to the Rend characteristic of its melee weapons for the rest of the turn.

In addition to these Armies of Renown, you also get five Regiments of Renown all based around legendary Sons of Behemat who’ve been known to work with factions across the Mortal Realms:

  • Odo Godswallow fights alongside DESTRUCTION armies – A Beast-smasher Mega-Gargant especially effective against Monsters.

  • Bundo Whalebiter works with ORDER and DESTRUCTION armies – A Kraken-eater Mega-Gargant smart enough to pull off a cunning trap.

  • One-eyed Grunnock battles with CHAOS and DESTRUCTION armies – A Warstomper Mega-Gargant who disrupts enemy attacks with seismic stomps.

  • Big Drogg Fort-Kicka accompanies DEATH and DESTRUCTION armies – A Gatebreaker Mega-Gargant with breath that can literally kill.

  • Krong the Club can be used by ANY army – A Mancrusher Gargant whose own body is a lethal crushing weapon.


Between them, you can field a Mega-Gargant in any army in the game, so if you ever feel the need for some extreme damage to back up your disciplined Ossiarch legions or reaving Idoneth Deepkin, there’s a Regiment of Renown for you.

The new Battletome: Sons of Behemat goes up for pre-order this Saturday, alongside the new Ma Maegran and Boss-stompers kits and the riotously fun Brawlers of Behemat box set. If you want to find out how that game of titanic duels between Mega-Gargants plays, come back tomorrow and we’ll tell you.

* We covered the difference between Big and Little units in our look at the Sons of Behemat army rules.
** Fancy collecting a Stomper Tribe army? There’s a new themed box set up for pre-order soon that’ll get you started.
